scenes.heading: Choosing the right social platforms for a client instead of all of them

sents.d: Choosing the right social platforms for a client instead of all of them
Managing five platforms poorly serves a client worse than managing two platforms well.

Recommending every available platform to a new client often serves your invoice better than it serves their actual business — a local service business rarely needs deep TikTok investment, for instance, while it might badly need a well-maintained Google Business Profile presence.
Asking where the client's actual customers already spend time, rather than defaulting to whatever's currently trendy, leads to a platform mix that's more likely to produce real business results.

It's usually better to propose doing fewer platforms well than to spread a limited budget or your own time thin across many platforms mediocrely — this also tends to produce better results you can point to in reporting.

take: Recommend the platforms their customers actually use.
